status: FROZEN before any six-hour, lead-by-lead score of these models existed. The SHA-256 of this file is recorded in the commit that froze it. Amendments only before any result is seen.
title: Does the heavy-rain gain hold from +6 to +36 h? Six-hour rain, lead by lead.
origin: Every fine-tuned arm trains with a rollout of one six-hour step; Bris itself was trained with a rollout of six. Every heavy-rain result so far is one number for the 06-06 UTC day ending at +30 h, which mixes the steps ending at +12 to +30 h. If the gain came from the one step the loss rewards, it would be largest early and shrink with lead. This scores each six-hour step separately, out to +36 h, the last step the later arms were forecast to.

models.baseline: plain Bris as MET released it, ~/bris-runs/evaluation/baseline
models.control2000: control arm without the spectral term
models.controlfft2000: control arm with Bris' spectral term, the comparator
models.meps15: all fifteen MEPS members valid from 00 UTC (scripts/fetch_meps_members.py)

period: test year, 00 UTC cycles 2025-08-01 to 2026-09-06, four members per Bris model
truth: hourly Frost gauges (observations/precipitation.npz) summed over the six hours ending at each valid time; only complete windows; gauges flagged by scripts/check_gauges.py left out; isolated large hours it lists are kept, as in every hourly score so far. Model value from the nearest cell, within 5 km.

cases.models: a gauge and cycle is kept only if the observation and every Bris model are present at every one of the six leads, so each lead is scored on the same gauge-cycles
cases.with_meps: the same, further restricted to gauges and cycles where all fifteen MEPS members are present at every lead (the MEPS files hold only the daily-network gauges, so fewer stations)

calibration: month-out isotonic, fitted per model, per lead and per threshold; month of the cycle
bootstrap: paired, seven-day blocks of cycle dates, so every lead of a cycle stays in one block; 5000 replicates

primary_endpoint.measure: Brier score at 10 mm per 6 h after calibration, at +36 h, tailC2000 minus controlfft2000, case set 'models'
primary_endpoint.why_10_mm: exceeded in 1.3 percent of six-hour gauge windows, about as rare as 20 mm in a day (1.4 percent of gauge-days), the threshold of every result so far
primary_endpoint.positive_if: the upper 95 percent bound is below 0: Pavo still better at the last lead
primary_endpoint.negative_if: the lower 95 percent bound is above 0

key_secondary.measure: the same difference at +36 h minus that at +12 h, per gauge-cycle, bootstrapped the same way
key_secondary.why_these_two: both windows are 06-12 UTC, one day apart, so the contrast is lead and not time of day
key_secondary.shrinks_if: the lower bound is above 0 (the advantage is smaller at +36 h than at +12 h)

secondary_reported: every lead and every threshold, each Bris model against controlfft2000, calibrated and raw, with Brier skill score and ROC area
fair CRPS of all rain per lead, each model against controlfft2000
case set 'with_meps': each Bris model against meps4 per lead, and the skill of meps15 beside them
not_claimed: Hourly automatic gauges are a different network from the daily climate gauges every result so far used, and carry more faults. One start time, 00 UTC. Leads only to +36 h: the +54 h day exists for plain Bris and the first arms, not these. One draw of each model.
